policy_name: AI Guidelines for Business (AI事業者ガイドライン), Version 1.2
issuing_authority: Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications (MIC) and Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI), Japan
regulatory_regime: Japanese soft-law AI governance (alongside the AI Promotion Act)
geo_constraints: Businesses developing, providing or using AI in Japan; voluntary

locale_context.regulation: Soft law · non-binding business guidelines (living document)
locale_context.culture: Japanese soft-law, consensus-oriented governance: voluntary, multi-stakeholder 'agile governance' with responsibilities split across developers, providers and business users.

key_dates.event: Version 1.0 published (integrating earlier MIC AI R&D/Utilization Guidelines and METI AI Governance Guidelines)
Version 1.2 published (adds AI agents and physical AI; revises risk-based approach and actor categories)
MIC study materials discuss a further update (consideration stage, not adopted)

covered_systems: AI systems and services generally, including generative AI, AI agents and physical AI
exceptions: non-business (personal) use is out of scope
conditions: risk-based: measures proportionate to the magnitude and likelihood of harm
objective: Provide unified, living guidance so that businesses developing, providing and using AI can voluntarily manage risks and realise safe, secure and trustworthy AI while promoting innovation.

related_policies.policy: Governance Guidelines for Implementation of AI Principles ver. 1.1 (METI, 2022)

conflict_rule: Non-binding soft law; existing laws (e.g. APPI, Copyright Act) prevail.

sources_consulted: https://github.com/suwa-sh/zenn-contents/blob/main/articles/ai-business-guidelines_20260803.md (secondary summary of v1.2: 3 actors, 3 basic philosophies, 10 common guiding principles) - fetched
record_provenance.notes: policy_id retains '2024' (first version); record describes the latest Version 1.2 (2026-03-31). METI/MIC sites were blocked, so no clause could be quoted verbatim; all clauses are paraphrases. Version history dates (v1.01 Nov 2024, v1.1 2025-03-28, v1.2 2026-03-31) are from secondary sources. Basic philosophies: human dignity, diversity & inclusion, sustainability. METI/MIC published English versions of earlier editions; whether an official English version of v1.2 exists was not verified, so official_languages lists only ja. Exact section numbering of v1.2 not verified.

clauses.section: Main text, Part 2 - Common guiding principles: Human-centric
clauses.original_text: Each actor should, when developing, providing or using AI, act so as not to infringe the human rights guaranteed by the Constitution or internationally recognised, and should respect human dignity and autonomy, including avoiding AI that unduly manipulates human decision-making or emotions.
clauses.actor: AI developers, providers and business users
clauses.action: respect human rights, dignity and autonomy
clauses.requirement: human-centric design and use of AI
clauses.interpretation_notes: Paraphrase, not verbatim: the official document could not be fetched from the compilation environment (issuer site blocked by network policy); content reconstructed from secondary summaries and compiler knowledge. Original is Japanese; English wording is the compiler's, not METI/MIC's official English version. Section labels approximate.

clauses.section: Main text, Part 2 - Common guiding principles: Safety
clauses.original_text: Each actor should avoid harm to the lives, bodies, property and minds of stakeholders and to the environment throughout the AI lifecycle, including by ensuring appropriate data quality, operating AI within its intended scope and enabling human judgement or control where necessary.
clauses.actor: AI developers, providers and business users
clauses.requirement: lifecycle risk management to avoid harm
clauses.purpose: prevent physical, psychological, property and environmental harm
clauses.interpretation_notes: Paraphrase, not verbatim: the official document could not be fetched from the compilation environment (issuer site blocked by network policy); content reconstructed from secondary summaries and compiler knowledge. clauses.section: Main text, Part 2 - Common guiding principles: Transparency
clauses.original_text: Each actor should, to a reasonable extent and in light of the technical characteristics and social context of the AI, ensure verifiability and provide stakeholders with appropriate information, such as the fact that AI is being used, its intended use, data collection policies and limitations.
clauses.actor: AI developers, providers and business users
clauses.action: provide information; keep logs for verifiability
clauses.requirement: disclose AI use and relevant characteristics; maintain verifiability

clauses.section: Main text, Part 2 - Common guiding principles: Accountability
clauses.original_text: Each actor should, to a reasonable extent, fulfil accountability for its AI, including ensuring traceability, clarifying responsibilities and points of contact, documenting its governance approach and explaining it to stakeholders.
clauses.actor: AI developers, providers and business users
clauses.requirement: accountability and traceability across the AI value chain

clauses.original_text: Businesses deploying AI agents should set the agent's permissions appropriately and build in safeguards, including human judgement or approval where necessary, to prevent risks such as erroneous autonomous actions (e.g. mistaken bookings).
clauses.actor: AI providers and business users of AI agents
clauses.requirement: appropriate permission scoping and human involvement for autonomous AI agents
clauses.condition: when AI agents act autonomously on behalf of users
clauses.purpose: prevent harmful or erroneous autonomous actions
